subject.title: [Bug]: agents set-identity --workspace does not set the agent's stored workspace, but its success response implies it does

question: Should the public `openclaw agents` CLI solve existing-agent workspace relocation with a dedicated setter/update command, or should this issue be fixed only by clarifying that `set-identity --workspace` is a locator and adjusting its output?
rationale: Both repairs are technically viable, but they change public CLI semantics or JSON output compatibility differently, so automation should not choose the product contract on its own.

options.title: Add Dedicated Setter
options.body: Add a documented `agents update --workspace` or `agents set-workspace` command that uses the existing Gateway update path, while making `set-identity` output explicit about locator versus stored workspace.

options.title: Clarify Locator Only
options.body: Keep relocation out of the CLI for now and add additive output/docs changes so `set-identity` cannot be mistaken for a stored-workspace update.

options.title: Repurpose Set Identity
options.body: Make `set-identity --workspace` update the stored workspace too, accepting the compatibility risk against current help text and docs.

recommendation.title: Add Dedicated Setter
recommendation.body: Add a documented `agents update --workspace` or `agents set-workspace` command that uses the existing Gateway update path, while making `set-identity` output explicit about locator versus stored workspace.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the public agent CLI contract introduced with the identity helper and not just the lower-level Gateway implementation.
